motion: Do we need God for morality?

moves.currentDescription: Ferrer replies that reason and external data remain interpreted through the same brain whose reliability is under examination and cannot escape it.
moves.lockedProposition: Reason and external data cannot escape the circularity problem because access to both remains filtered through the same brain under examination.

moves.currentDescription: Dillahunty argues that incompatible first person revelations cannot resolve disagreement and do not repair motivation objections made against secular morality.
moves.lockedProposition: First-person revelation neither resolves conflicting divine claims nor fixes the disagreement and motivation problems raised against secular morality.
